THE RULE THIS TABLE EXISTS TO KEEP: A class is a claim about what a city's own law says. It is NOT inferred from a search summary, and it is NOT inferred from the fact that a parcel carries a district code.
`unclassified` is a legitimate value and is used below for six cities. A city that cannot be classified at source stays unaccounted and is named. It is never guessed into a class.

Why that rule has teeth here more than usual: setbackCellMayBeMoved releases only `unaccounted` cells, so every cell this lane would write as refused, absent-verified or value is STICKY. A city wrongly classed (b) freezes a fabricated default onto its parcels and no later correction can move it.

unclassified.detail: This is the ONE city in the sweep whose evidence actively suggests a non-(a) class, and it is therefore the most important unresolved row. Thrall publishes development ordinances covering 'setbacks, minimum living space, sign ordinance, manufactured homes, adoption of the code' -- development standards without any published zoning-district list or zoning map. Williamson County's official Thrall map shows city boundaries and NO zoning districts, while the same county's Florence map is published alongside Florence's separate zoning apparatus. A city whose setback rules live in a development ordinance with no districts is the (c)/(b) shape.
unclassified.needed: read the Thrall 'packet of Ordinances for permit and planning process' linked from http://cityofthrall.com/departments/development_permits.php and determine whether it establishes districts at all. If it does not, Thrall is class (c) or a (b) default -- and either answer changes a city from refused to absent-verified or to a served value.

unclassified.detail: The top result for 'City of Crawford Texas zoning' is crawfordNE -- the City of Crawford, NEBRASKA. The retrieved ordinance PDF says in its own text 'the City of Crawford, Nebraska' and 'within the one-mile area of planning and zoning jurisdiction set forth by Nebraska law'. Its districts (R-1, R-2, C-1, C-2, I, A) are Nebraska law. Attributing them to Crawford, McLennan County, Texas would import another state's statute into a Texas setback table.
unclassified.needed: a direct read of Crawford's Texas code of ordinances or contact with Crawford City Hall, McLennan County (254-486-2125).

Creedmoor, Texas is a separate city in Travis County with its own government.
unclassified.needed: a direct read of Creedmoor, Texas's ordinances (cityofcreedmoortx.gov) or the Travis County record.

theSixUnresolvedCities: ALL SIX have the same resolution, and it is one this session could not perform: read the city's own code, or ask the city. Three of them (mart, crawford, creedmoor) have a WORSE failure mode than 'not yet read' -- a keyword search returns a DIFFERENT CITY, and for two of those the different city is in a different STATE. Those three are the ones most likely to be guessed wrong by a successor who searches the same way.
NONE of the six may be written as refused or absent-verified on the evidence above. All six stay `unaccounted`.
Class distribution of the six is unknown and should not be assumed: thrall's evidence points to (c)/(b), granger's and hallsburg's to (a), and the three false-positive cities to nothing at all.

theThreeFalsePositiveCities_namedForTheR.trapShape: A city name that is not unique across the United States, where the highest-authority-looking result is the wrong namesake. The wrong city's districts are internally consistent and look authoritative, so nothing about the retrieved text signals the error except the state, the county, the highway names, or the agency acronyms.
theThreeFalsePositiveCities_namedForTheR.mart-tx: vs MARTINDALE, TX -- same state, neighbouring county (Caldwell), and Martindale is IN this lane's six-county set. A same-state trap with no state mismatch to catch it; the only tell is that the result names the wrong city outright.
theThreeFalsePositiveCities_namedForTheR.crawford-tx: vs CRAWFORD, NE -- the retrieved ordinance PDF states 'City of Crawford, Nebraska' and cites Nebraska law in its own text.
theThreeFalsePositiveCities_namedForTheR.creedmoor-tx: vs CREEDMOOR, NC -- zip 27522, Granville County GIS, NCDEQ, and districts named after North Carolina highways (US 15, NC 56).
theThreeFalsePositiveCities_namedForTheR.operationalRule: For any city in this lane, a source is admissible only if it names the city AND the correct Texas county, or is the city's own .gov/.us/.org domain with a Texas address. A .gov domain is NOT sufficient: cityofcreedmoor.org and the Crawford NE revize site both look official and are both the wrong municipality.
